title: Conventions of the Cloud Connector API capture: base path, default responses, paging and decoding

prose.text: The captured Cloud & Branch Connector contract is a reconstruction of the vendor's published reference, and some of its structure is an artifact of that capture. This subject records the conventions an agent needs before reading a path or a response schema from it.

prose.label: Base path.
prose.text: {{oneapi-base-path}} The hosts and sign-in for each path are in [[cloud-connector.api.authentication]].

prose.label: OneAPI Postman collection.
prose.text: {{postman-base-variable}} {{postman-oneapi-only-notes}} The provider documentation carries the same note for DNS and log rules only: [[cloud-connector.terraform.provider-config:dns-log-rules-oneapi-only]]. {{postman-ztgateway-not-in-contract}} Zero Trust Gateways themselves are described in [[cloud-connector.overview.zero-trust-gateways]].

prose.label: Success responses.
prose.text: {{default-response-as-success}} {{default-as-success-marker}} Which status code those operations return on success, and whether the default schema is a success body at all, is open {{gap:default-response-semantics}}.

prose.label: Paging.
prose.text: The Go SDK's list helper for ZTW requests 1000 items a page and stops at the first shorter page: [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:ztw-stops-on-page-shorter-than-1000]], with the truncation risk in [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:ztw-capped-page-truncates]].

prose.label: Decoding.
prose.text: The Go SDK decodes a ZTW create response into its typed object only when the Content-Type is exactly JSON: [[shared.sdk-go.request-handling:ztw-create-requires-exact-content-type]].

checks.do: Before treating a status code from the captured ZTW contract as the operation's success code, whether that operation's response is the reconstructed default response.
Before calling a `/ztGateway` path, that it comes from the Postman collection only: the captured contract and the clients have no Zero Trust Gateway endpoints to check it against.

oneapi-base-path.statement: The captured contract's server is `https://api.zsapi.net/ztw/api/v1`, so its paths (such as `/ecRules/ecRdr`) sit under `/ztw/api/v1` on api.zsapi.net.

default-response-as-success.statement: The structural validation report of the OpenAPI snapshot counts 165 Cloud & Branch Connector operations on 96 paths and flags 124 of them with the issue `default_response_as_success`.

quotes: | `zcloudconnector` | 165 | 96 | 124 | current public route table |
- `default_response_as_success`: 124

default-as-success-marker.statement: In the contract those operations carry `x-zscaler-default-as-success` and a `default` response, with no 200 or 204 response; the activate operation is one of them.

postman-base-variable.statement: The OneAPI Postman collection sets `ZTWBaseUrl` to `{{oneAPIBaseUrl}}/ztw/api/v1`, and has folders named `Cloud & Branch Connector` and `Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector`.

postman-ztgateway-not-in-contract.statement: The Postman collection has a `Zero Trust Gateway` folder of `/ztGateway` requests (list, create, update, delete, lite, count, status, config status and compare, events, license info, supported regions and traffic tests), and the captured OneAPI contract has no `/ztGateway` path; the Cloud & Branch Connector release notes for July 06, 2026 announce these endpoints as new.
postman-ztgateway-not-in-contract.conditions: Absence: the contract's /paths was checked for the /ztGateway paths; under vendor/ the string ztGateway occurs only in the Postman collection and that release note, so no captured SDK, Terraform provider or MCP source calls these endpoints either.

default-response-semantics.title: Success status and body of the ZTW operations whose contract has only a default response
default-response-semantics.detail: The contract keeps method, path and field metadata for these operations, but a reconstructed default response does not show which 2xx status the API returns on success, or whether the embedded schema is the success body rather than a catch-all envelope.
default-response-semantics.blocks: asserting a success status code or response body for most ZTW operations from the contract alone
